h1: Axion About — AI & SaaS About Page Design
tagline: “Through research, creative thinking and iteration we help growing brands realize their digital full potential” — the whole about page is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: About page reference for an AI or SaaS product — cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) easing, fluid type, #F26522 accent and a 640x468 frame.
about: Axion About keeps its decision trail: the brief that produced this about page runs 4,393 characters. It leads with “Through research, creative thinking and iteration we help growing brands realize their digital full potential” and gives that line the frame rather than shrinking it into a card. The whole page is built on white #EDEDEE underneath, deep red #3E3133 for the type and bright orange #F26522 carrying the accents. The build is React and Tailwind CSS; every measurement in it is written down, which is what makes it reusable. Motion comes down to cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1). If you are briefing a SaaS about page, start from this composition and replace the subject.

layout.title: The spacing steps are quoted
layout.body: The layout works on absolute values rather than ratios: type from 12px to 18px, 12px spacing steps and cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) easing. Because the values are fixed, a substitution changes the look without changing the rhythm.

layout.title: Badge above the fold
layout.body: The announcement is a #F26522 pill above the headline, sized below the supporting copy so it reads as a label rather than a second title. The badge carries #F26522 while the headline stays on the ink colour.

layout.title: The composition is the content
layout.body: The composition is complete at 640x468: the copy, the media and the controls are all named in the brief. The page is one composition at 640x468, which is why it holds together when the copy changes.

layout.title: Nothing here is inherited
layout.body: Spacing is quoted the same way (type from 12px to 18px, 12px spacing steps and cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) easing), not as a scale that grows on its own.

motion.title: Interaction is on the controls
motion.body: The interactive layer is small and predictable: hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card. Everything else stays still, which keeps the emphasis on the composition. Press states are specified as well as hover, so a tap gives the same confirmation as a click. A few reliable states beat a long list of effects.

motion.title: Short, matched timings
motion.body: Transitions are specified at 0 using cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1), which is the timing the controls are held to. Because the values are short, a rebuild that slows them down is immediately visible.

fonts.name: Face not specified
fonts.role: The brief fixes the type scale but leaves the face to the build

notes: Accent and ground are both named (bright orange #F26522 on white #EDEDEE), so a brand swap moves one value.
Accent use is limited to bright orange #F26522; everything else sits on white #EDEDEE.
The accent is spent on bright orange #F26522 and the rest of the composition holds white #EDEDEE.

Hold the about page to one screen on desktop; the brief never asks the reader to scroll past the fold.

editorial.title: How Axion About sequences the first read
editorial.body: The trade-off is patience: the page withholds the detail a scannable grid would hand over immediately. What it buys is a first screen where the announcement badge and the stats row cannot be misread. A SaaS reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: What holds up for AI & SaaS
editorial.body: Axion About works because its hierarchy is decided rather than decorated. The brief sets type from 12px to 18px, 12px spacing steps and cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) easing, so new copy lands inside the frame instead of reopening it. Axion About states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: Making the about page yours
editorial.body: The composition is the reusable part; the subject is yours. Swap the headline, keep the type scale (type from 12px to 18px), and re-test the #F26522 accent over your own media. If a new element does not help explain the offer or the next action, it belongs below the fold. Keep the media crop; it is doing as much work as the type.

faq.question: What does the brief behind Axion About actually contain?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 4,393 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: Why does the entry name React and Tailwind CSS at all?
faq.answer: Axion About was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Can I keep the Axion About transitions and change the timings?
faq.answer: Transitions are attached to interface states rather than to a scroll timeline, and they resolve in the sub-second range using cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1). The brief records the values so a port can match them without guessing.

audience: This about page is built for agencies that need the 640x468 frame to survive three rounds of client edits.
